description: A specialized yoga practice focused entirely on structural alignment, biomechanics, and precision in postures. Unlike fast-paced flows, this class holds poses longer and frequently utilizes props like blocks, straps, and blankets to help participants achieve optimal skeletal alignment regardless of their natural flexibility. It emphasizes body awareness, corrective posture work, and balancing muscle groups, making it excellent for long-term joint health and spinal decompression.
primary_benefit: Postural correction and flexibility
contraindications: Generally safe, but inform the instructor of acute joint inflammation or recent herniated discs.
interesting_fact: Holding poses with proper alignment can often feel more physically challenging than moving quickly, as it forces stabilizing muscles to work continuously.

description: Also known as Aerial Yoga, this practice utilizes a soft fabric hammock suspended from the ceiling to support the body's weight. By counteracting gravity, it allows participants to perform advanced stretching and inversions without compressing the spine or putting pressure on the joints. The class combines traditional yoga poses with elements of pilates, dance, and calisthenics, suspended mid-air.
primary_benefit: Spinal decompression and core strength
contraindications: Avoid if you have high blood pressure, glaucoma, or are pregnant, due to frequent inverted positions.
interesting_fact: Being upside down in the hammock trickles fresh oxygenated blood to the brain, providing an instant natural mental clarity boost.

description: A high-energy, music-driven water aerobics class conducted in chest-deep water. It eliminates the rhythmic choreography of traditional dance classes, focusing instead on continuous aquatic movements like water-resisted punching, high knees, and jumping jacks. The water acts as a natural 360-degree resistance mechanism, challenging the cardiovascular system while keeping joint impact practically non-existent.
primary_benefit: Cardiovascular fitness without joint strain
contraindications: Safe for most, but individuals with open wounds or severe water phobias should avoid.
interesting_fact: Water resistance provides up to 12 times the resistance of air, making simple movements surprisingly exhausting.

description: An intense underwater running workout, typically performed in deep water using buoyancy belts or flotation vests to keep the head above water. Participants mimic an aggressive running gait against fluid resistance without ever hitting a hard surface. This environment isolates the lower body muscles, building massive running-specific endurance and strength while entirely eliminating the jarring impact forces associated with road running.
target_age_group: All ages (Highly utilized by injured runners)
primary_benefit: Aerobic conditioning and lower body endurance
contraindications: Inability to swim comfortably in deep water without panic.
interesting_fact: Professional marathon runners frequently use deep-water running to maintain their elite cardiovascular fitness while recovering from stress fractures.

description: A foundational strength-training session focused exclusively on mastering basic compound movements using standard Olympic bars and plates. The workout revolves around the core lifts: back squats, overhead presses, deadlifts, and bench presses. It emphasizes progressive overload, safety, lifting mechanics, and building functional raw strength rather than rapid pacing or high-cardio conditioning.
primary_benefit: Muscular strength and bone density
contraindications: Avoid or modify heavily if suffering from acute disc herniations or severe shoulder impingement.
interesting_fact: Barbell exercises trigger a higher neuroendocrine response (testosterone and growth hormone release) than isolation machines because they recruit multiple joints at once.

description: A high-energy, sports-inspired cardio workout by Les Mills. It combines athletic aerobic movements like running, lunging, and jumping with strength exercises such as push-ups and squats. Set to motivating, high-bpm music, this class is structured around high-intensity intervals designed to maximize stamina, speed, agility, and overall athletic performance.
primary_benefit: Stamina and cardiovascular endurance
contraindications: Not recommended for individuals with severe knee osteoarthritis or acute shin splints.
interesting_fact: A single Body Attack class can rack up over 8,000 steps, making it an incredible tool for overall daily movement goals.

description: A Les Mills program that beautifully blends elements of Yoga, Tai Chi, and Pilates into a seamless, music-driven flow. The class begins with controlled Tai Chi movements to warm up the body, progresses into a challenging yoga and pilates sequence to build core strength and flexibility, and concludes with guided meditation and relaxation. It is a structured way to lower stress levels while strengthening the stabilizing muscles.
primary_benefit: Flexibility, core strength, and stress reduction
contraindications: Generally safe; third-trimester pregnant women should take modified options for abdominal tracks.
interesting_fact: The class is timed precisely to specific tracks of music to foster a seamless emotional and physical flow state.

description: An explosive, non-contact martial arts fitness program choreographed by Les Mills. Participants draw from disciplines like Boxing, Kickboxing, Muay Thai, Karate, and Taekwondo to punch, kick, and strike their way through an intense cardio session. The workout challenges the core and lower body continuously due to the rotational mechanics of throwing strikes against air resistance.
primary_benefit: Cardiovascular health and upper body conditioning
contraindications: People with chronic shoulder dislocations or severe hip limitations should monitor strike extensions closely.
interesting_fact: Because there is no physical punching bag, your core muscles have to work twice as hard to decelerate your arms and legs during rapid strikes.

description: The original barbell class designed to lean out, tone, and strengthen the entire body using 'The Rep Effect.' Rather than lifting heavy weights for a few repetitions, participants utilize light-to-moderate weights on adjustable barbells to perform roughly 800 repetitions across a single 55-minute session. Each major muscle group is isolated to its own dedicated, high-tempo music track.
primary_benefit: Muscular endurance and body composition styling
contraindications: Individuals with severe tendinitis or acute back spasms should use minimal plate weight.
interesting_fact: A single Bodypump track can feature up to four consecutive minutes of continuous squatting or pressing without a break.

description: A premium dance workout created by Les Mills that merges the latest electronic dance music, hip-hop, and house tracks with complex, stylistic choreography. The class is broken up into blocks of movement blocks that gradually layer on top of each other until a massive, full-length routine is completed. It is designed to be an emotional and artistic release through raw movement.
primary_benefit: Cardio endurance and rhythm development
contraindications: Not recommended for individuals who experience dizziness, severe coordination challenges, or major ankle instability.
interesting_fact: The choreographers for Body Jam often collaborate with world-renowned backing dancers to bring authentic street style into commercial commercial gyms.

description: An advanced adaptation of the standard Bodypump format. Rather than following high-speed musical tempos with light weights, this class reduces the speed and repetition counts while drastically increasing the barbell load. It is designed for gym-goers who enjoy a structured group class atmosphere but want to focus on progressive hypertrophy and muscular strength, moving closer to traditional weight room guidelines.
primary_benefit: Muscle hypertrophy and maximum power generation
contraindications: Not suitable for total beginners or individuals dealing with unmanaged joint degeneration.
interesting_fact: This class serves as a direct gateway for people transitioning from light group exercise over to serious individual powerlifting routines.

description: A high-performance indoor cycling class using specialized Keiser bikes equipped with magnetic resistance flywheels. These bikes track metric outputs like real-time wattage, RPMs, and energy expenditure. The class focus is strictly data-driven performance, mimicking authentic road-biking conditions like steep mountain climbs, pacing strategies, and power intervals to push boundaries.
primary_benefit: Cardiovascular power and quad/glute endurance
contraindications: Safe for bad joints, but people with severe heart conditions should monitor target heart zones closely.
interesting_fact: Unlike traditional spinner bikes, Keiser bikes use eddy-current magnetic fields to create resistance, meaning the workout stays completely smooth even under intense force.

description: A military-style group fitness class that features rapid transitions between aerobic and strength intervals. Participants are constantly shifted between bodyweight exercises (burpees, push-ups, planks) and functional equipment training (sandbags, battle ropes, medicine balls). It is fast, challenging, and often incorporates team building or partner activities to foster accountability.
primary_benefit: Fat loss and full-body conditioning
contraindications: Avoid if suffering from severe spinal issues, wrist pain (due to high volume push-ups/planks), or joint issues.
interesting_fact: Bootcamps mimic basic military training structures to create a high-bonding environment that keeps members consistent.

description: A hyper-targeted lower body class focused strictly on developing strength, size, and shape in the gluteal muscle complex. Workouts focus primarily on hip thrusts, cable kickbacks, Bulgarian split squats, and resistance band abductions. It skips upper body work entirely to ensure maximum mechanical tension and cellular fatigue can be forced onto the hips and hamstrings.
primary_benefit: Glute hypertrophy and hip stability
contraindications: Individuals dealing with acute lower back or hip labral tears need strict modifications.
interesting_fact: Strengthening the glutes directly treats lower back issues, as they are the primary anchors for stabilizing your pelvis.

description: A hybrid functional workout designed to bring commercial gym trainees closer to multi-joint cross-training. It eliminates rigid, single-muscle machine tracking, opting instead for structural complexes involving kettlebell swings, rowing machines, sled pushing, and dumbbell carries. It delivers high athletic conditioning while prioritizing safety and technique adjustments.
primary_benefit: All-around functional athletic conditioning
contraindications: Not ideal for people struggling with dynamic balance or acute rotator cuff injuries.
interesting_fact: This class bridges the gap between commercial weight machines and hardcore functional clubs.

description: A classic stationary indoor cycling class that focuses on endurance base building, rhythm spinning, and aerobic efficiency. Trainees ride along with an instructor simulating flat roads, rolling hills, and long steady climbs. It focuses on steady-state cardiorespiratory health, making it highly accessible to beginners and seasoned lifters looking to optimize recovery flow.
primary_benefit: Aerobic base building and low-impact leg endurance
contraindications: People with acute lower back pain should ensure professional bike saddle setup to prevent slouching.
interesting_fact: Steady-state cycling can build cellular mitochondrial health without inducing muscle soreness, making it a great pairing for heavy leg lifting days.

description: A brutal, highly concentrated stationary bike workout based entirely on High-Intensity Interval Training. The session avoids long, steady efforts, focusing instead on max-effort sprints (such as 20–30 seconds of flat-out pedaling at maximum resistance) followed by brief rest intervals. It is designed to rapidly spike the heart rate, shocking the metabolic system to burn maximum calories in a short timeframe.
primary_benefit: Anaerobic capacity spike and rapid caloric burn
mental_focus: Overcoming maximum lactic acid burning comfort
contraindications: Unmanaged high blood pressure or significant cardiovascular historical concerns.
interesting_fact: Due to EPOC, your metabolism remains highly elevated and burns extra fat for up to 24 hours after finishing a 30-minute Cycling HIIT class.

description: A dynamic fitness class catered to female biomechanics and specific aesthetic training goals. The programming seamlessly fuses light aerobic endurance blocks with bodyweight core styling, high-rep limb conditioning, and light resistance tracks. It emphasizes lean muscle stamina, metabolic speed, and a highly supportive group atmosphere.
primary_benefit: Muscular endurance, posture development, and agility
contraindications: Safe across a broad demographic, but notify of any pelvic floor or lower back flare-ups.
interesting_fact: This class structures its pacing to deliver an athletic, full-body sweat without overloading vulnerable connective joints.

description: A dedicated strength and resistance training class tailored for women who want to master free weights, dumbbells, and barbells. This workout ditches high-impact cardio jumping, focusing instead on progressive compound lifting, muscle hypertrophy, and structural form. It emphasizes developing a powerful physique, boosting metabolic health, and building bone density through serious resistance.
primary_benefit: Muscle definition, skeletal strength, and empowerment
contraindications: Requires proper form tracking for individuals with pre-existing spinal herniations.
interesting_fact: Lifting heavy weights will not make women 'bulky' due to natural hormone balances; instead, it develops lean muscle mass and burns dense body fat efficiently.

description: A long-duration conditioning class designed to increase aerobic capacity and mental stamina. The programming utilizes rowing machines, stationary assault bikes, ski-ergometers, and light bodyweight circuits. Workouts are structured into long blocks (10-20 minutes of continuous effort) designed to keep the heart rate inside Zone 2 and Zone 3 to maximize fat oxidation.
primary_benefit: Aerobic threshold advancement and stamina
contraindications: People suffering from acute, unmanaged chronic fatigue syndrome should proceed with caution.
interesting_fact: Building a solid endurance engine makes your high-intensity recovery time significantly shorter during heavy lifting sessions.

description: Short for 'Gimnasia de Rehabilitación' (Rehabilitation Gymnastics), this is a therapeutic class overseen by fitness professionals specializing in injury management. The movements are highly controlled, incorporating isometric holds, resistance bands, and mobility tools. It is designed to rebuild muscle activation, fix asymmetrical joint movement, and safely return injured individuals to mainstream fitness.
target_age_group: All ages (Highly recommended for seniors and recovery stages)
primary_benefit: Joint rehabilitation and pain-free biomechanics
contraindications: Requires direct clearing by a medical doctor or physical therapist if recovering from recent surgery.
interesting_fact: The class focuses heavily on deep stabilizing muscles, like the rotator cuff and transversus abdominis, which are often missed in traditional training.

description: A technical class dedicated to Olympic Weightlifting, focusing on the Snatch and the Clean & Jerk. The workout breaks down these complex movements into parts, using PVC pipes and technical barbells to build speed, explosive power, mobility, and coordination. It trains the body to generate maximum explosive force from the floor to overhead in fractions of a second.
primary_benefit: Explosive athletic power and functional mobility
contraindications: Avoid if dealing with severe wrist limitations, advanced shoulder instability, or poor thoracic extension.
interesting_fact: Olympic lifters possess some of the highest vertical jumps of any athletes in the world due to their incredible rate of force development.

description: An adult gymnastics and bodyweight mastery class focusing on core control, spatial awareness, and upper body pulling and pressing power. Trainees utilize rings, parallel bars, stall bars, and floor work to develop skills like handstands, pull-ups, muscle-ups, and L-sits. It builds an incredible strength-to-weight ratio while dramatically expanding wrist and shoulder mobility.
primary_benefit: Relative strength, core compression, and deep balance
mental_focus: Balance, body coordination, and overcoming fear
contraindications: Avoid if suffering from severe chronic wrist impingements or inner-ear vertigo issues.
interesting_fact: Gymnastics ring training forces your body to constantly stabilize in three dimensions, recruiting nearly double the muscle fibers of fixed gym bars.

description: The foundation of modern yoga, Hatha involves a gentle, deliberate sequence of physical postures (asanas) combined with conscious breathing techniques (pranayama). Poses are held for several deep breaths, allowing beginners to learn proper alignment, build foundational muscular endurance, and cultivate mental stillness. It focuses on balancing opposing energies in the body through sustained physical postures.
primary_benefit: Stress relief, balance, and basic flexibility
contraindications: Highly safe; accessible to individuals with minor physical limitations.
interesting_fact: In Sanskrit, 'Ha' means sun and 'Tha' means moon, symbolizing the practice's goal of balancing active and passive internal energies.

description: A high-intensity, music-driven boxing and martial arts conditioning class that uses heavy bags, MMA gloves, and medicine balls. Unlike non-contact formats, HBX Round focuses on delivering physical strikes against heavy resistance bags. This provides a massive full-body workout, blending punching combinations, kickboxing intervals, and explosive core conditioning.
primary_benefit: Cardiovascular stamina and explosive upper/lower body power
impact_level: Medium to High-impact (Impact through wrist/shin strikes)
contraindications: People with severe wrist arthritis or unmanaged carpal tunnel syndrome should use caution.
interesting_fact: Striking a heavy bag requires your core to contract instantly on impact to absorb the shock, building deep abdominal strength.

description: A contemporary fitness class that combines strength training and cardiovascular endurance within a single session. Trainees alternate between structural barbell or dumbbell lifting blocks (such as heavy lunges or rows) and intense cardiovascular conditioning blocks (like running, rowing, or skiing). It is designed to build an athletic, well-rounded physique by preventing the body from adapting to just one style of training.
primary_benefit: Concurrent conditioning (strength and stamina)
mental_focus: Managing energy pacing across different modalities
contraindications: Requires careful pacing for individuals returning from chronic overtraining syndrome.
interesting_fact: Hybrid training is the fastest-growing sector in modern fitness, mirroring the functional demands of everyday life.

description: The advanced version of the standard Hybrid class. It features heavier lifting targets, longer cardio blocks, and shorter recovery intervals. It is designed for seasoned athletes or high-level fitness enthusiasts looking to push their aerobic and anaerobic thresholds to their absolute limits in a demanding, high-intensity environment.
primary_benefit: Peak athletic output and elite mental toughness
mental_focus: Extreme grit and handling physical fatigue
contraindications: Strictly not for beginners or individuals with underlying cardiac or structural joint issues.
interesting_fact: Hybrid Max workouts often mimic the volume and intensity seen in professional tactical athlete training protocols.

description: A cardio-focused conditioning class specifically engineered to build the aerobic capacity needed for Hyrox races. The class skips heavy lifting and instead features high-volume intervals on rowing machines, ski-ergometers, and stationary bikes, mixed with running blocks. The goal is to build an elite aerobic engine capable of sustaining effort for over an hour.
primary_benefit: Aerobic threshold expansion and running stamina
contraindications: People with acute Achilles or calf injuries should monitor repetitive running and machine strokes.
interesting_fact: Hyrox races are roughly 50-60% running, meaning an efficient 'cardio engine' is the single biggest factor in lowering finish times.

description: A high-energy, social fitness session designed to introduce gym members to the fundamentals of Hyrox racing. It features partner workouts, team relays, and scalable team workouts utilizing basic Hyrox tools like wall balls, kettlebells, and rowing machines. It prioritizes team camaraderie, making functional fitness accessible and fun.
primary_benefit: Teamwork, motivation, and basic functional work
contraindications: Easily scalable, but notify of any significant lifting restrictions.
interesting_fact: Working out in a group team environment has been shown to increase physical output by up to 20% due to positive peer accountability.

description: A strength-focused Hyrox class designed to tackle the heavy stations of the global competition. The class isolates and targets the leg and core strength required for the heavy Sled Push, Sled Pull, Farmers Carry, and heavy Sandbag Lunges. It combines explosive leg power with grip strength and core bracing under fatigue.
primary_benefit: Leg drive power, grip strength, and core bracing
contraindications: Avoid if suffering from acute lower back pain or severe knee joint degeneration.
interesting_fact: The Sled Push in Hyrox requires moving up to 175kg (including the sled), making specialized leg drive training essential.

description: A technical workshop class focused on mastering the mechanics, pacing strategy, and transitions of Hyrox fitness racing. Instructors break down individual movements—such as the exact foot placement for Burpee Broad Jumps or optimal rowing stroke efficiency—to help participants save energy and improve performance. It functions like a sports lab focused on efficiency.
primary_benefit: Biomechanical efficiency and race strategy
contraindications: Accessible to anyone planning to run a Hyrox or functional competition.
interesting_fact: Slightly adjusting your technique on movements like Wall Balls can save valuable energy and shave minutes off your total race time.

description: A specialized running class designed specifically for the unique demands of a Hyrox race. It simulates 'compromised running'—the difficult transition of running immediately after your legs are fatigued from heavy leg exercises like sled pushes or lunges. Trainees mix track or treadmill running intervals with short bursts of bodyweight or leg fatigue movements.
primary_benefit: Compromised running adaptation and pacing control
mental_focus: Overcoming heavy leg fatigue while running
contraindications: Not recommended for individuals recovering from recent knee joint injuries or plantar fasciitis.
interesting_fact: Running with legs full of lactic acid requires specific neural adaptations that can only be built through compromised running practice.

description: A physically demanding, structured class inspired by traditional Ashtanga Yoga. It features a specific, continuous sequence of postures synchronized with deep belly breathing (Ujjayi pranayama). This practice builds internal heat, detoxifies muscles, and develops core strength, flexibility, and upper body stamina through continuous sun salutations and transitions.
primary_benefit: Upper body pressing strength, flexibility, and stamina
contraindications: Individuals with unmanaged carpal tunnel syndrome or severe wrist issues will struggle with the constant weight-bearing positions.
interesting_fact: Traditional Ashtanga is practiced in silence without music, turning the sound of the class breathing into a collective meditation.

description: A highly scientific, 30-minute core conditioning workout created by Les Mills (formerly known as CxWorx). Using resistance tubes, weight plates, and bodyweight movements, it targets the entire midsection, including the abs, glutes, back, and stabilizing muscles. It is designed to improve functional strength, balance, and injury prevention.
primary_benefit: Core stability, posture alignment, and lower back health
mental_focus: Strict muscle isolation and bracing technique
contraindications: Acute lower back disc issues require modified options for the twisting tracks.
interesting_fact: This class targets the 'anatomy of the core' as a single system, connecting the shoulders down to the hips rather than just working the upper abs.

description: A high-energy, accessible dance fitness workout designed by Les Mills. It features standalone tracks set to global hits, mixing dance genres like hip-hop, house, and contemporary style. Unlike older formats, the steps are easy to follow, making it a great cardio workout for people who want to burn calories through expressive movement without feeling overwhelmed by complex choreography.
primary_benefit: Cardiovascular conditioning and coordination
contraindications: Safe for most, but individuals with severe ankle instability should take care during quick lateral steps.
interesting_fact: The movements are designed to be intuitive, allowing participants to focus on a high-cardio sweat rather than perfect dance technique.

description: A foundational mind-body system focused on deep core strength, postural alignment, and muscular balance. Performed on mats using bodyweight and tools like magic circles or resistance bands, exercises focus on controlled, precise movements initiated from the 'Powerhouse' (the deep core muscles between the ribs and pelvis). It emphasizes core control and length rather than muscle bulk.
primary_benefit: Core strength, spinal alignment, and flexibility
contraindications: Highly versatile; excellent for injury recovery when movements are modified.
interesting_fact: Pilates was originally called 'Contrology' by its creator, Joseph Pilates, because it requires complete mental control over every muscle group.

description: A fitness-focused, faster adaptation of traditional yoga. It combines athletic flow sequences with strength exercises like lunges, push-ups, and core work. Rather than holding gentle stretches, this class moves quickly from pose to pose, creating a cardiovascular challenge while building lean muscle strength and flexibility.
primary_benefit: Lean muscle strength, flexibility, and cardio endurance
contraindications: Not recommended for individuals with acute wrist injuries or severe rotator cuff issues.
interesting_fact: Power Yoga was popularized in the West during the 1990s specifically to make yoga more appealing to traditional fitness and gym enthusiasts.

description: Short for 'Recovery,' this class is designed to help the nervous system reset and muscles recover from intense training. It combines active mobility work, gentle stretching, foam rolling (myofascial release), and guided breathing techniques. The goal is to lower cortisol levels, reduce muscle soreness, and transition the body into a relaxed, restorative state.
primary_benefit: Nervous system recovery and reduced muscle soreness
contraindications: Accessible to everyone, regardless of fitness level or injuries.
interesting_fact: This class helps switch the nervous system from the 'fight or flight' sympathetic state into the 'rest and digest' parasympathetic state, accelerating muscle repair.

description: A high-energy functional strength class centered around the gym's main functional frame or structural rig. Workouts incorporate hanging movements (to build grip and upper body pull strength), suspension trainers (TRX), landmine presses, and wall balls. It blends strength and coordination in an engaging, athletic format.
primary_benefit: Functional upper body strength and core control
contraindications: Avoid if dealing with acute shoulder impingements or severe wrist issues.
interesting_fact: Using suspension trainers on the rig forces the core to engage constantly to maintain stability throughout every movement.

description: An indoor, group treadmill coaching class designed to improve cardiorespiratory health and running technique. The instructor guides participants through speed changes, incline intervals, and pacing strategies set to high-energy music. It is a structured way to build running endurance without being affected by outdoor weather conditions.
primary_benefit: Cardiorespiratory health and running technique
contraindications: Not recommended for individuals with severe knee joint degeneration or acute shin splints.
interesting_fact: Modern treadmills feature cushioned decks that absorb up to 30% of the impact force compared to running on hard concrete or asphalt roads.

description: A strength and resistance class specifically designed for adults over the age of 50. It focuses on functional movement patterns (such as sitting down and standing up safely, carrying objects, and overhead reaching) using light-to-moderate dumbbells, resistance bands, and machines. The class prioritizes joint safety, longevity, and maintaining physical independence.
primary_benefit: Maintaining bone density, muscle mass, and joint stability
contraindications: Accessible, but individuals with severe osteoporosis should inform the instructor to modify spinal rotation exercises.
interesting_fact: Regular resistance training after age 50 is the most effective way to combat sarcopenia, the natural loss of muscle mass that occurs with aging.

description: A gentle strength and balance class designed for seniors aged 60 and over. It focuses heavily on improving balance, coordination, core stability, and functional muscle strength to prevent falls and maintain joint mobility. It utilizes light hand weights, resistance loops, and chair-supported options to ensure safety and comfort.
primary_benefit: Fall prevention, joint mobility, and physical independence
contraindications: Safe for most, but individuals with severe inner-ear issues should use chair-supported options for balance.
interesting_fact: Strength training over 60 has been shown to improve cognitive function and memory by stimulating the production of brain-derived neurotrophic factor (BDNF).

description: A scientific strength training class created by Les Mills. Unlike high-rep classes like Bodypump, this program focuses on slower tempos, heavier weights, and lower repetition ranges (such as 8–12 reps). It follows structured phases of hypertrophy, pure strength, and power development, making it an excellent bridge to independent weight room training.
primary_benefit: Muscle hypertrophy and maximum lifting power
contraindications: Not recommended for individuals with acute joint inflammation or poor lifting form.
interesting_fact: This program was designed based on sports science research to deliver the benefits of heavy gym lifting within an organized group fitness format.

description: An intense strength class based on traditional Strongman training. Participants learn to lift, carry, and push heavy, unusual objects like stones, sandbags, logs, and axle barbells. It builds powerful core strength, grip endurance, and explosive power, utilizing functional movement patterns that challenge the entire body.
primary_benefit: Maximum raw strength and explosive power
contraindications: Strictly avoid if you have chronic lower back pain, disc issues, or severe joint degeneration.
interesting_fact: Lifting awkward, uneven objects like sandbags engages more stabilizing core muscles than lifting balanced, symmetrical gym barbells.

description: A dynamic, flowing style of yoga that links breath directly with movement. Participants move smoothly through a creative sequence of postures (such as sun salutations, standing balances, and backbends), using transitions to build internal heat, cardiovascular stamina, flexibility, and core strength.
primary_benefit: Flexibility, core strength, and moving meditation
contraindications: People with acute shoulder or wrist injuries should take modified options for downward dogs and planks.
interesting_fact: The word Vinyasa can be translated as 'to place in a special way,' referring to the deliberate, mindful progression of poses.

description: Short for 'Workout of the Day,' this is a core high-intensity cross-training class. Every day features a new combination of movements, mixing Olympic lifting, gymnastics skills, and high-intensity cardio intervals (like rowing or skipping). Workouts are performed against the clock or for maximum repetitions, pushing participants to their athletic limits.
primary_benefit: All-around athletic conditioning and functional power
contraindications: Not recommended for individuals with acute joint injuries or poor baseline movement mechanics.
interesting_fact: The variety in daily WODs prevents the physical adaptation plateaus common in repetitive training routines.

description: A high-intensity Workout of the Day (WOD) performed in pairs or teams of three or four. Participants split the required repetition volume (such as 100 kettlebell swings or a 2km row) among teammates, strategizing on how to share the workload effectively. It combines intense conditioning with high-energy communication and teamwork.
primary_benefit: Conditioning, teamwork, and high-volume pacing
mental_focus: Team strategy and communication under fatigue
contraindications: Easily scalable, but participants should communicate any movement restrictions to their teammates.
interesting_fact: Team WODs are highly popular because splitting high repetition counts allows individuals to maintain a faster pace during their active intervals.

description: A balanced yoga practice that combines active and passive styles. The first half of the class (the Yang) features an active, heat-building Vinyasa flow to strengthen muscles and improve circulation. The second half (the Yin) transitions to passive, deep floor stretches held for several minutes to target the deep connective tissues and fascia, promoting relaxation.
primary_benefit: Muscle strength, joint flexibility, and nervous system balance
mental_focus: Balancing active energy with deep patience
contraindications: Generally safe; individuals with hypermobility should avoid overstretching during the passive Yin phase.
interesting_fact: This class mirrors the concept of duality, helping participants build physical strength while cultivating deep mental calmness.

description: Also known as 'Yogic Sleep,' this is a deeply meditative, low-intensity practice performed entirely while lying comfortably in a supported savasana position. Guided by the instructor, participants go through body scans and visualization techniques to enter a deep state of conscious relaxation between waking and sleeping. It focuses on stress relief, mental recovery, and emotional balance.
primary_benefit: Stress reduction, improved sleep quality, and mental recovery
contraindications: Accessible to everyone, including individuals with severe physical injuries or limitations.
interesting_fact: A single 45-minute session of Yoga Nidra is said to provide the restorative benefits of up to three hours of deep sleep.

description: A high-energy, cardio dance class that features Latin and international music rhythms. It mixes low-intensity and high-intensity moves into an interval-style dance party designed to burn calories while boosting coordination and mood. The choreography includes elements of salsa, merengue, reggaeton, and cumbia, making cardio fitness accessible and fun.
primary_benefit: Cardiovascular fitness, coordination, and mood boost
contraindications: Safe for most, but individuals with severe knee or ankle instability should modify high-impact twisting movements.
interesting_fact: Zumba was created in Colombia during the 1990s when an instructor forgot his regular aerobics music and used his personal Latin music tapes instead.

description: A functional class designed to improve active joint range of motion, movement control, and flexibility. Unlike passive stretching, it emphasizes controlling muscles at their end ranges of movement using bodyweight exercises and mobility tools. It targets tight hips, shoulders, and thoracic spines to improve overall movement quality and prevent training injuries.
primary_benefit: Active range of motion, joint health, and injury prevention
contraindications: Accessible to everyone; excellent for lifters, runners, and sedentary office workers.
interesting_fact: Improving mobility helps you lift heavier weights safely by allowing you to reach deeper, more efficient positions in exercises like squats and overhead presses.
